findings.evidence: Lines 459-463 give the general boost version; lines 533-539 give only `(orientation (Fin 2)).areaForm (transversePart (transverseIsometry R b)) (relativeTransverse (transverseIsometry R k) (transverseIsometry R P))`. Mathlib's `Orientation.areaForm_comp_linearIsometryEquiv` (mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/TwoDim.lean:157) makes the general version a one-line rewrite, as it already is at line 538.
findings.fix: Add `areaForm_relativeTransverse_transverseIsometry (R) (hR) (b k P)` with `relativeTransverse b P` in the first slot, proved by `rw [relativeTransverse_transverseIsometry, relativeTransverse_transverseIsometry, Orientation.areaForm_comp_linearIsometryEquiv _ R hR]`, and derive the current `transversePart` form from it via `relativeTransverse_of_plusComponent_eq_zero` (or keep the current one, which needs no hypothesis, as a separate corollary of `transversePart_transverseIsometry`).
findings.issue: For boosts the PR proves the general `areaForm_relativeTransverse_transverseBoost` (both slots `relativeTransverse _ P`) and derives the `transversePart` case at line 468. The isometry side only has the mixed special case `ω(transversePart b, relativeTransverse k P)`; the parallel general statement `ω(relativeTransverse b P, relativeTransverse k P)` is never stated, so a user who needs the rotation analogue of the general boost lemma has to redo it.

findings.evidence: Lines 429-431: the whole proof is `rw [sub_eq_add_neg, transverseBoost_add]`; `transverseBoost_symm` (line 424) already rewrites `(transverseBoost v).symm` to `transverseBoost (-v)`, so the stated RHS is the unsimplified side of an existing simp lemma. No other declaration in the PR uses it.
findings.fix: Either drop it, or state the form that does add content: `transverseBoost (u - v) = (transverseBoost v).symm.trans (transverseBoost u)`, using `transverseBoost_symm`.
findings.issue: `transverseBoost_sub u v : transverseBoost (u - v) = (transverseBoost (-v)).trans (transverseBoost u)` is literally `transverseBoost_add u (-v)` after `sub_eq_add_neg`; its right-hand side is not reduced to anything the `add` lemma does not already give, so it is duplicate API with no added content.

summary: Assumptions are load-bearing and the orientation file sits at the right level, but the isometry half of the §0.1 invariance is proved only in a narrower special case than its boost counterpart, and `transverseBoost_sub` restates `transverseBoost_add` with nothing added.
